newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pacific BBA sees higher 97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pacific BBA sees higher 97 earnings.

text.p: Automotive parts manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd said on Tuesday it expected increased earnings from all divisions in 1997.
"The overall outlook for Pacific BBA is excellent," Pacific BBA Managing Director Barry Jackson said in the group's 1996 results statement.
"We are looking forward to increased earnings from all divisions in 1997," he said.
Earlier, Pacific BBA reported a 6.1 percent rise in net profit for the year to A$16.87 million and kept its final dividend unchanged at eight cents per share.
It said its net profit before abnormal items fell to A$23.76 million from A$25.28 million in 1995.

There was an abnormal loss after tax of A$6.9 million, including A$1 million from the unsuccessful offer for Azon Ltd AZO.AX and a A$5.9 million loss from the partial sale and writedown of its investment in Indonesian plastics manufacturer PT Dynaplast.
Pacific BBA said the 1996 result was satisfactory given the weakness of the Australian economy.

"While the Australian market was soft, the company's growing markets in Asia and North America contributed significantly to the result with 22 percent of sales and 34 percent of operating profit coming from businesses outside Australia," Jackson said.
He said the group's plastics business had continued to expand in the Asia Pacific region, but experienced flat demand in Australia during the second half after the strong first half.
"The plastics division is planning to increase its presence in Asia through expansion of existing business and pursuit of new opportunities, particularly in industrial packaging," Pacific BBA said.

"In Australia, the division will introduce a new range of materials handling products and will concentrate on achieving better returns from its automotive and industrial operations in Victoria and South Australia," it said.
Pacific's PBR automotive unit would lift export volumes, while completion of the new plant in Tennessee would be a key priority, it said.
The construction products division would commission its Philippines plant during 1997 and was well advanced with plans for two new plants in Asia.
Pacific BBA's shares were up two cents at A$4.30 at 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT).
